nodes.text: 13C NMR indicates compound has both aromatic and aliphatic components

support.quote: The 13C NMR spectra provide chemical shifts that suggest the presence of aromatic carbons (around 160.80, 135.43, 130.70, 130.40, 128.70, 128.35, 124.85 ppm) and aliphatic carbons (57.20, 41.00, 39.20, 34.00, 24.56, 19.40, 16.60 ppm). This indicates a compound with both aromatic and aliphatic components.

nodes.text: 1H NMR confirms aromatic protons and aliphatic groups (methyl, methylene, methine)

support.quote: The 1H NMR spectra indicate the presence of aromatic protons (7.04 ppm), which aligns with the aromatic carbons observed in the 13C NMR. The signals at 1.12 ppm (doublet), 2.04 ppm (doublet of doublets), 2.21 ppm (singlet), 2.34 ppm (singlet), 2.70 ppm (doublet of doublet of quartets), and 4.01 ppm (doublet of doublets) suggest the presence of aliphatic protons, possibly indicating methyl, methylene, and methine groups.

nodes.text: IR spectra: broad peak at 3357 cm⁻¹, C-H stretches ~3000 cm⁻¹, C=C stretches at 1606 and 1587 cm⁻¹
IR broad peak at 3357 cm⁻¹ indicates O-H stretch (alcohol or phenol); 1606/1587 cm⁻¹ indicate aromatic C=C

support.quote: The IR spectra show a broad peak at 3357 cm⁻¹, which is indicative of an O-H stretch, suggesting the presence of an alcohol or phenol group. The peaks around 3000 cm⁻¹ are typical of C-H stretches in aromatic and aliphatic compounds. The peaks at 1606 and 1587 cm⁻¹ suggest C=C stretches, which are consistent with aromatic rings.
